## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Recommendation accounts for a major sparse-ML systems workload class.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Contrasts embeddings and categorical features with dense networks. |
| **Systems behavior** | Sparse embedding lookups, memory capacity, and dense-sparse interaction. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | Direct inheritance from the MLPerf Inference v1.0.1 recommendation workload. |
| **Model choice** | MLPerf Inference v1.0.1 fixes the official 40-million-entry checkpoint for the accuracy run. |
| **Dataset choice** | The official inference accuracy recipe fixes Criteo Terabyte and its unshuffled day 23 evaluation data. |
| **Quality metric** | MLPerf Inference v1.0.1 publishes 80.25% ROC AUC for the official model and evaluator. |
| **Published baseline** | Official MLPerf Inference v1.0.1 DLRM quality result |
| **Alternative rejected** | MovieLens micro-DLRM changes both task scale and upstream contract. |

## Current Preflight and Handoff

::: {.callout-warning}
**The quality path is not a general local run yet.** Run the pinned accuracy adapter in a 256-GB-class environment with the manually licensed Criteo data and official 40M checkpoint.
The `max` and `pro` runners fail closed until the declared assets, hardware, and runtime are available. Use `doctor` to inspect the machine-readable environment handoff.
:::

```bash
# inspect the authoritative environment handoff
uv run mlperf doctor --workload recommendation --profile max --format json

# preview asset requirements without downloading
uv run mlperf fetch --workload recommendation --profile max --dry-run

# the bounded functional path runs on supported local hardware
uv run mlperf run --workload recommendation --profile min
```

A successful `min` result verifies the local plumbing only. It does not evaluate the authoritative quality target. See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for the current local-execution boundary and recovery status.

## Results

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload recommendation --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.
